ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies the two jugulars with the span between the throat and the two collarbones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو ما بين الحلقوم والعلباوين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r6.speaker: الأثرم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r6.claim: Al-Athram calls the jugular the body's river and lists the names of major veins in different body parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r6.anchor: وقال الأثرم: هو نهر الجسد، هو في القلب: الوتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes the jugulars as two veins flanking the front of the neck and connecting to the aorta; he explains the name by the spirit's passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p526#2/r7.anchor: والوريدان عرقان مكتنفان بصحفتي العنق في مقدمها متصلان بالوتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r7.claim: الإنسان may denote the human species generally or Adam specifically.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r8.claim: God's nearness is nearness in knowledge of the person and his states, not spatial presence; حبل الوريد is an image for extreme closeness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p532/r8.anchor: قرب علم به وبأحواله، لا يخفى عليه شيء من خفياته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p533/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p533/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p533/r1.claim: Ḥabl al-warīd is a vein named by comparison to a cord; the phrase is explanatory, or may mean the cord at the shoulder, which shares the neck region with the jugular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p533/r1.anchor: والحبل: العرق الذي شبه بواحد الحبال، وإضافته إلى الوريد للبيان

STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r9.claim: The surah moves from rejection of the Prophet and resurrection, through creation and past peoples, to death, the Hereafter, mindfulness of death, and a final reminder.
STUDYQURAN:50:intro/r9.anchor: the sūrah calls one to reflect upon the wonders of creation as evidence of God’s Omnipotence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r4.claim: God’s knowledge and creative power establish resurrection, and He has secured the record of human deeds and utterances.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p434/r4.anchor: The Almighty’s attributes of Knowledge and Creativity which prove the certainty of the Day of Judgement

RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r1.claim: One reading makes human creation a fresh proof following 50:15, where the earlier creation means the heavens.
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون ابتداء استدلال بخلق الإنسان ، وهذا على قولنا { أفعيينا بالخلق الاول } ( ق: 15 ) معناه خلق السماوات

RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r2.claim: Another reading treats the clause as completing the account of human creation, with the earlier creation referring to humanity's first creation.
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r2.anchor: وثانيهما : أن يكون تتميم بيان خلق الإنسان ، وعلى هذا قولنا الخلق الأول هو خلق الإنسان أول مرة

RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r3.claim: The statement may also warn people to turn back from their claims, since God knows every hidden matter and what lies within their breasts.
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r3.anchor: تنبيه على أمر يوجب عودهم عن مقالهم ، وبيانه أنه تعالى لما قال : { ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه }

RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r4.claim: The jugular is the vein through which blood runs to every part of the body; although flesh conceals it, nothing conceals anything from God's knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r4.anchor: والوريد العرق الذي هو مجرى الدم يجري فيه ويصل إلى كل جزء من أجزاء البدن

RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r5.claim: The comparison expresses the perfection of God's knowledge: bodily tissue may hide a vein, but nothing can hide from divine knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r5.anchor: والله أقرب من ذلك بعلمه ، لأن العرق تحجبه أجزاء اللحم ويخفى عنه ، وعلم الله تعالى / لا يحجب عنه شيء

RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, nearness may refer to God's exclusive power over the person, with His command governing him as blood moves through his veins.
RAZI-FULL:v28p140#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال { ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد } بتفرد قدرتنا فيه يجري فيه أمرنا كما يجري الدم في عروقه

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r1.claim: Al-insān means man or the human being as such.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r1.anchor: Man translates al-insān, which also means the human being as such.

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r2.claim: Some understand the human being as Adam and the verse as God's knowledge of his inclination to eat what was forbidden.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r2.anchor: some understand it as a reference to Adam and God’s knowledge of his inclination to eat of what had been forbidden to him (Q)

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r3.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r3.claim: Most take the phrase to mean that God knows what lies within people and the true intentions behind their words and actions, even when they themselves are unaware.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r3.anchor: Most, however, see it as a reference to God’s Knowledge of all that lies within breasts

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r4.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r4.claim: An alternative reading takes the phrase to say that God knows what the soul whispers.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r4.anchor: The second phrase could also be read, “and We know that of which his soul whispers” (Aj).

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r5.claim: Many commentators find the statement of nearness problematic and seek to avoid its literal meaning.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r5.anchor: We are nearer to him than his jugular vein is problematic for many commentators.

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r6.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r6.claim: Some commentators say “We” refers to the two angels, thereby avoiding a literal reading of divine nearness.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r6.anchor: Some seek to avoid the literal meaning, saying that “we” refers to two angels (IK).

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r7.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r7.claim: Others connect the phrase to the next verse: God's nearness holds when the two receivers arrive, and He remains powerful over them and needs no angels to know human actions.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r7.anchor: He is not in need of them in order to know what the person is doing (Z).

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r8.claim: The author sees the verse as affirming God's immanence throughout creation: Divine Reality underlies every reality and is nearest to each human being; God is with people wherever they are.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r8.anchor: this is one of several verses that indicate the Immanence of God in all of creation (see, e.g., 2:115)

STUDYQURAN:50:16/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r9.claim: Although God is always close, people often fail to be close to Him and so remain far away.
STUDYQURAN:50:16/r9.anchor: human beings, nonetheless, often fail to be with or close to God and thus remain far from Him.

TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r1.claim: God knows what a person inwardly tells himself, so none of the person's secrets or heart's thoughts are hidden from Him.

TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r2.claim: The warid is a vein between the throat and collarbones; habl and warid name the same vein, joined in an expression using two different names.
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد} [ق: 16] يقول: «عرق العنق»

TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the vein as the one in the throat.
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، {حبل الوريد} [ق: 16] قال: الذي يكون في الحلق

TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the warid as the neck vein.
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد} [ق: 16] يقول: «عرق العنق»

TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r5.claim: One Arabic interpretation takes God's nearness to mean that He has greater mastery and power over the person.
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r5.anchor: فقال بعضهم: معناه: نحن أملك به، وأقرب إليه في المقدرة عليه

TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r6.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r6.claim: Another Arabic interpretation takes the nearness to mean that God knows the person's inward whisper better.
TAB-FULL:v21p421#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: {ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد} [ق: 16] بالعلم بما توسوس به نفسه

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r1.claim: Al-Kashifi says Meccan polytheists admitted God originated creation: whoever can create without material or aid can surely recreate people from matter and restore their lives, though Satanic whispers make resurrection seem contrary to custom and prompt doubt.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r1.anchor: قال الكاشفي : مشركان مكه معترف بودند بانكه حق تعالى مبدع خلق است

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r2.claim: The indefinite خلق magnifies the new creation, marks its departure from customary limits, and signals that it merits serious inquiry rather than neglect.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r2.anchor: وتنكير خلق لتفخيم شأنه والإشعاد بخروجه عن حدود العادات

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r3.claim: Sufis and theologians hold that new creation occurs continually in worldly bodies and accidents: both substances and accidents may cease each instant while seeming persistence comes from renewed similars.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r3.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الخلق الجديد حاصل في الدنيا أيضا سواء كان في الأعراض أو في الأجسام

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r4.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r4.claim: The Mathnawi’s verses portray forms and speech emerging from the formless and thought, then returning to their source, like renewed waves and life continually arising anew.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r4.anchor:
قال في المثنوي :
صورت از معنى وشيراز يشه دان
ياوآ واز وسخن زانديشه دان

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿrani says the world changes every breath and never remains unchanged for an instant; change is in attributes rather than entities, so God creates continually.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r5.anchor: قال الإمام الشعراني رضي الله عنه في كتاب الجواهر تقليب العالم واقع في كل نفس

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r6.claim: This doctrine explains reports that the Kaaba circumambulates certain men and turns toward them, as happened with Rabiʿa al-Adawiyya; its truth requires full unveiling from God.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r6.anchor: ومنه يعرف طواف الكعبة ببعض الرجال واستقبالها لهم كما وقع ذلك لرابعة العدوية رضي الله عنها وغيرها

BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r7.claim: The phrase means what the self inwardly tells itself or what crosses the mind; waswasa is a hidden sound or a bad thought, like the faint tinkling of jewelry.
BURSEVI:v9p89#2/r7.anchor: {ولقد خلقنا الانسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه} أي ما تحدث به نفسه وهو ما يخطر بالبال والوسوسة الصوت الخفي والخطرة الرديئة

BURSEVI:v9p90/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p90/r1.claim: If ما is relative, the pronoun refers to it and باء is like in ‘he whispered it’; if مصدرية, the pronoun returns to the human and باء is causative, since the self makes him one who experiences whispering.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r1.anchor: والضمير لما أن جعلت موصولة والباء كما في صوت بكذا وهمس به يعني أنها صلة

BURSEVI:v9p90/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r2.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v9p90/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes ما as مصدرية because Arabic says a person told himself something, as well as that his self told it to him.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r2.anchor: قال في الكشاف ما مصدرية لأنهم يقولون حدث نفسه بكذا كما يقولون حدثته به نفسه

BURSEVI:v9p90/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p90/r3.claim: God knows a person before creation with essential knowledge and after creation with actual knowledge; inner thoughts too are created by God and cannot be hidden from their Creator.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى كما يعلم حال الإنسان قبل خلقه علما ثبوتيا كذلك يعلمه بعد خلقه علما فعليا

BURSEVI:v9p90/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p90/r4.claim: The self’s whispers include appetites, bad character, corrupt belief, and other traits that distract the heart and its present moment.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r4.anchor: ودخل فيما توسوس به نفسه شهواته المطلوب لاستيفاؤها وسوء خلقه واعتقاده الفاسد

BURSEVI:v9p90/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p90/r5.claim: Adam is included: God knew the thought by which he ate from the tree, which came through Satan’s prompting.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r5.anchor: وفيه دخل آدم عليه السلام فإن الله تعالى خلقه وعلم ما وسوست به نفسه في أكل الشجرة

BURSEVI:v9p90/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v9p90/r6.claim: Some gnostics say Satan cannot reach prophets’ inner selves: their thoughts contain no satanic share, since he approaches only through outward senses, and they do not act on his suggestions.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r6.anchor: قال بعض الكبار ليس للشيطان على باطن الأنبياء من سبيل

BURSEVI:v9p90/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p90/r7.claim: Some saints are protected from Satan’s suggestions, but not from his reaching their hearts; unlike prophets, saints do not legislate, whereas prophetic inner selves are protected because they bear revealed law.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r7.anchor: ثم إن من الأولياء من يحفظ من الشيطان في علم الله تعالى فيكون بهذه المثابة

BURSEVI:v9p90/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r8.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v9p90/r8.claim: Some gnostics say every person has exactly 70,000 daily thoughts, matching the angels entering the Frequented House; each thought creates an angel who ascends, joins those angels, and intercedes for its person, while every heart remains inhabited and each thought-angel takes a fitting form in God’s knowledge.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r8.anchor: قال بعض الكبار ما في شخص من بني آدم إلا ويخطر له كل يوم سبعون ألف خاطر

BURSEVI:v9p90/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p90/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p90/r9.claim: The pronoun refers to the human: God is nearer to him than his jugular vein.
BURSEVI:v9p90/r9.anchor: {ونحن أقرب إليه} أي إلى الإنسان {من حبل الوريد} ازرك جان وى بوى

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines waswasa as a bad, fleeting thought, deriving it from waswas, the sound of jewelry or a faint whisper.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r3.anchor: قال الراغب الوسوسة الخطرة الرديئة وأصله من الوسواس

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r4.claim: Creating the human means his ongoing, changing existence, not only his initial formation; every creature that persists continually depends on its Lord.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r4.anchor: والمراد بخلق الإنسان وجوده المتدرج المتحول خلقا بعد خلق

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r5.claim: The present-tense knowledge clause signals continuity alongside the past-tense but continuing act of creation.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r5.anchor: وهو فعل مضارع مسوق للدلالة على الاستمرار على قوله

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r6.claim: The statement of nearness likewise conveys permanence and continuity for as long as the human exists.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r6.anchor: مفيد للثبوت والدوام والاستمرار باستمرار وجود الإنسان

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r7.claim: The verse links to the argument from God's knowledge and power in first creation in 50:6 and to the preceding doubt about a new creation in 50:15.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r7.anchor: اتصال بما تقدم من الاحتجاج على علمه وقدرته تعالى في الخلق الأول

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r8.claim: The verse establishes God's direct knowledge of the human and, through guardian angels, knowledge of his acts; awareness of inner whispering signals knowledge of all outward and inward states.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r8.anchor: فهي في سياق يذكر قدرته على الإنسان بخلقه

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r9.claim: The hidden thought includes a skeptic's doubt about resurrection: how can a person be raised after death has scattered the body into indistinguishable dust?
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r9.anchor: ومما توسوس به الشبهة في أمر المعاد كيف يبعث الإنسان

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r10.claim: Here mā is a relative pronoun, the pronoun in bihi refers to it, and the preposition means instrument or cause.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r10.anchor: عائد إليه والباء للآلة أو للسببية

TABATABAI:50:15-16/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r11.claim: The verse attributes whispering to the self rather than Satan, though Satan also whispers, because it discusses God's encompassing knowledge of the human and his innermost thoughts.
TABATABAI:50:15-16/r11.anchor: ونسب الوسوسة إلى النفس دون الشيطان وإن كانت منسوبة إليه أيضا

TABATABAI:50:16-18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r1.claim: The warid is a blood-carrying vein distributed through the body; another view identifies it as the vein in the throat. It is called a cord by comparison, and the genitive is explanatory.
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r1.anchor: الوريد عرق متفرق في البدن فيه مجاري الدم

TABATABAI:50:16-18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r2.claim: God is nearer to a person than the vein running among his organs inside the body, so He fully knows him and his inner thoughts.
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r2.anchor: المخالط لأعضائه المستقر في داخل بدنه فكيف لا نعلم به

TABATABAI:50:16-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r3.claim: The familiar image is an easy approximation for ordinary understanding, while God's actual nearness is vastly greater.
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r3.anchor: وهذا تقريب للمقصود بجملة ساذجة يسهل تلقيها لعامة الأفهام

TABATABAI:50:16-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r4.claim: God made the human a soul and ordered its effects; He mediates between the soul and itself and between it and its actions, nearer than anything one can posit, even the self.
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r4.anchor: فهو الواسطة بينها وبين نفسها وبينها وبين آثارها وأفعالها

TABATABAI:50:16-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r5.claim: This subtle account of divine nearness is comparable to 8:24, which says God comes between a person and his heart.
TABATABAI:50:16-18/r5.anchor: وقريب منه بوجه قوله { إن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه }

TABRISI:50:12-20/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:12-20/r1.claim: Human being here means humankind collectively, the descendants of Adam.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r1.anchor: أراد به الجنس يعني ابن آدم

TABRISI:50:12-20/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:12-20/r2.claim: God knows what the heart thinks, conceals, and keeps within itself from other creatures.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r2.anchor: ما يحدث به قلبه وما يخفي ويكن في نفسه ولا يظهره

TABRISI:50:12-20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:12-20/r4.claim: The jugular is a vein that branches through the body and accompanies a person in all its parts.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r4.anchor: وهو عرق يتفرق في البدن يخالط الإنسان في جميع أعضائه

TABRISI:50:12-20/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:50:12-20/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the jugular as a vein in the throat.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r5.anchor: عرق الحلق عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:50:12-20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:50:12-20/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies it as a vein attached to the heart.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r6.anchor: عرق متعلق بالقلب يعني نحن أقرب إليه من قلبه عن الحسن

TABRISI:50:12-20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:50:12-20/r7.claim: One gloss says God knows a person better than someone who is as close to that person as the jugular vein.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r7.anchor: معناه نحن أعلم به ممن كان منه بمنزلة حبل الوريد في القرب

TABRISI:50:12-20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:50:12-20/r8.claim: Another gloss takes the nearness as God's greater mastery over the person, despite the vein's closeness.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r8.anchor: نحن أملك له من حبل وريده مع استيلائه عليه وقربه منه

TABRISI:50:12-20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:50:12-20/r9.claim: A further gloss says God is nearer in perception than the jugular would be, if it could perceive.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r9.anchor: نحن أقرب إليه بالإدراك من حبل الوريد لو كان مدركا

TABRISI:50:12-20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:12-20/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:12-20/r10.claim: God has assigned two angels to record deeds, establishing proof against each person.
TABRISI:50:12-20/r10.anchor: وكل به ملكين يحفظان عليه عمله الزاما للحجة

THALABI:v9p98/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p98/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p98/r1.claim: What the self whispers is what the heart tells itself; none of its secrets or inner thoughts are hidden from God.
THALABI:v9p98/r1.anchor: يحدثه قلبه، فلا يخفى علينا أسراره، وضمائره

THALABI:v9p98/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p98/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p98/r2.claim: God's nearness means that He knows and has power over the person more fully than the jugular vein; body parts can hide from one another, but nothing hides from God's knowledge.
THALABI:v9p98/r2.anchor: أي أعلم به، وأقدر عليه من حبل الوريد لأن أبعاضه، وأجزاءه يحجب بعضها بعضا،

THALABI:v9p98/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p98/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p98/r3.claim: The habal al-warid is the neck vein between the throat and the two collarbones; its plural is awrida.
THALABI:v9p98/r3.anchor: وحبل الوريد: عرق العنق، وهو عرق بين الحلقوم، والعلباوين، وجمعه أوردة،

THALABI:v9p98/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p98/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p98/r4.claim: The genitive construction 'the vein's cord' is an addition of a thing to itself, permitted because the two words differ.
THALABI:v9p98/r4.anchor: والحبل من الوريد وأضيف إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين، قال الشاعر:

THALABI:v9p98/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p98/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p98/r5.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses al-warid for the vein swelling with exertion, supporting the bodily sense of the term.
THALABI:v9p98/r5.anchor: والحبل من الوريد وأضيف إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين، قال الشاعر:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r1.claim: The human being here means the son of Adam, with الإنسان used as a generic noun.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r2.claim: The soul's whispering is what the heart speaks inwardly; God knows what a person conceals within, as in 7:20.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r2.anchor: يعني يحدث به قلبه. والمعنى: يعلم ما يخفي ويكن في نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r3.claim: Language scholars describe الوريد as a vein that branches through the body, with specific names for its upper-arm, forearm, hand, and inner-arm branches.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r3.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: الوريد: عرق تحت اللسان يتفرق في البدن، وهو في العضد فليق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r4.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r4.claim: Abu al-Haytham identifies the two veins beside the jugulars on either side of the throat notch; they pulse continuously, and he says a life-carrying vein carries breath rather than blood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم (¬5): الوريدان عرقان بجنب الودجين عن يمين ثغرة النحر ويسارها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r5.claim: Al-Layth says the two veins flank the sides of the neck, swell with anger, and are collectively called الأوردة or الورد.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r5.anchor: وقال الليث: هما وريدان مكتنفان صفحتي العنق، يقال للغضبان: قد انتفخ وريداه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r6.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r6.claim: Al-Farra, Abu Ubayda, and al-Zajjaj place the vein in the throat and inner neck.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r6.anchor: وذكر الفراء وأبو عبيدة والزجاج أن الوريد في الحلق وباطن العنق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r7.claim: Muqatil says the vein reaches the heart, while God's knowledge is nearer to the heart than that vein.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: هو عرق يخالط القلب، فعلم الرب تبارك وتعالى أقرب إلى القلب من ذلك العرق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r8.claim: The people of meaning interpret nearness as God's knowledge of the soul's thoughts: body parts may conceal one another, but nothing conceals anything from God's knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r8.anchor: قال أهل المعاني (¬4): المعنى: ونحن أقرب إليه في العلم وما تحدث به نفسه من هذا العرق المخالط للإنسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r9.claim: Although God knows the person inwardly, He assigns two angels to preserve and record the person's deeds as proof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p389/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر أنه مع علمه به وكل به ملكين يحفظان ويكتبان عليه عمله إلزاما للحجة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r3.claim: The soul's whisper is what the person's heart tells him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r3.anchor: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه } يحدثه قلبه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r4.claim: God is nearer to the person than the jugular vein by His knowledge; the vein is in the neck.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:14-19/r4.anchor: بالعلم { من حبل الوريد } وهو عرق في العنق

QASHANI:50:15-16/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:50:15-16/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:50:15-16/r4.claim: The vein is a sensory image for spiritual nearness, but bodily connection entails separation and two-ness; God's nearness and presence are not spatial contact or comparison.
QASHANI:50:15-16/r4.anchor: تمثيل للقرب المعنوي بالصورة الحسية المشاهدة

QASHANI:50:15-16/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:50:15-16/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:50:15-16/r5.claim: The human's embedded reality is not other than God; particular existence exists only through the divine reality of existence, without which it would be sheer nothingness.
QASHANI:50:15-16/r5.anchor: فإن هويته وحقيقته المندرجة في هويته وتحققه ليست غيره بل إن وجوده المخصوص المعين إنما هو بعين حقيقته التي هي الوجود من حيث هو وجود ولولاه لكان عدما صرفا

QASHANI:50:15-16/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:50:15-16/r6.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
QASHANI:50:15-16/r6.claim: Ali says God is with every thing without conjunction: a thing is itself through Him, and apart from Him there is no thing with which to compare Him.
QASHANI:50:15-16/r6.anchor: كما قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: " هو مع كل شيء "

ELMALILI:50:16/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r1.claim: His rendering emphasizes an oath by God’s majesty: We created the human and know its whispers, nearer than the jugular vein.
ELMALILI:50:16/r1.anchor: Meâl: Hem şânıma kasem ederim ki hakikat insanı Biz yarattık

ELMALILI:50:16/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r2.claim: Creation recalls the first creation, prepares what follows, and serves as an inference to God’s knowledge.
ELMALILI:50:16/r2.anchor: Bu ihtar hem halk-ı evveli takrir hem de mâba‘dine temhiddir, hem ilmin isbâtına halktan bir istidlâl

ELMALILI:50:16/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r3.claim: The creation reminder teaches transcendence so the statement of nearness does not confuse Creator and creature.
ELMALILI:50:16/r3.anchor: akrebiyetten bahsolunurken hâlık ile mahlûku karıştırmamak için bir tenzih delîlini telkindir

ELMALILI:50:16/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r4.claim: The soul’s whisperings include all inward consciousness: self-talk, feelings, imaginings, memories, fancies, and decisions.
ELMALILI:50:16/r4.anchor: gizli duygular, vehimler, hâtıralar, kuruntular, kararlar gibi bütün bâtınî şuur şuûnâtına şâmildir

ELMALILI:50:16/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r5.claim: God knows hidden thoughts unknown even to the recording angels, because He created them.
ELMALILI:50:16/r5.anchor: hafaza meleklerinin bile henüz vâkıf olmadığı derecede gizli olarak insanın gönlüne gelen hâtırat

ELMALILI:50:16/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r6.claim: God knows, reaches, and acts upon the human with the immediacy of nearness beyond the jugular.
ELMALILI:50:16/r6.anchor: Öyle yakından bilir, öyle yakından yetişir, icrâ-yı te’sîr ederiz

ELMALILI:50:16/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r7.claim: The Creator’s relation precedes the creature’s relation to itself, since the creature exists by God’s power; he links this to 2:186.
ELMALILI:50:16/r7.anchor: Hâlık ile mahlûku arasındaki nisbet, mahluk ile nefsi arasındaki nisbetten daha mukaddemdir

ELMALILI:50:16/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r8.claim: He distinguishes veins returning blood toward the heart from arteries carrying it outward, and describes black blood passing through the right heart and lungs, where it meets air and becomes red before returning to the left heart.

ELMALILI:50:16/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r9.claim: He calls the described circuits great and small circulation; arterial blood is red and venous black in the great circuit, reversed in the small.
ELMALILI:50:16/r9.anchor: Deverân-ı kebîrde şiryanlarda kırmızı, verîdlerde siyah kan vardır. Deverân-ı sağīrde ise şiryanlarda siyah

ELMALILI:50:16/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r10.claim: Thus red arterial and black venous blood are not universal labels; veins are black-blood vessels only generally.
ELMALILI:50:16/r10.anchor: verîdlere “siyah kan damarları” denmesi küllî değil, ekseriyet itibariyledir

ELMALILI:50:16/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r11.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:50:16/r11.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines the dual veridan as vessels along the front of the neck, connected to the vetin, carrying blood from the head.
ELMALILI:50:16/r11.anchor: Keşşâf’ta der ki: “El-verîdân boynun önünde iki safhasını kavramış iki damardır

ELMALILI:50:16/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r12.speaker: İbn Esîr
ELMALILI:50:16/r12.claim: Ibn al-Athir says the verid is a front-neck vessel that swells in anger; Elmalılı notes the jugular sense properly uses the dual.
ELMALILI:50:16/r12.anchor: İbn Esîr de Nihâye’de “verîd, boynun yüzündeki damardır ki gazab hâlinde şişer

ELMALILI:50:16/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r13.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:50:16/r13.claim: Raghib defines the verid as a vessel connected to the liver and heart, containing blood channels.
ELMALILI:50:16/r13.anchor: Nitekim Râgıb şöyle ifade etmiştir: “Verîd, kebide ve kalbe muttasıl olur bir damardır

ELMALILI:50:16/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r14.speaker: Nizamüddîn Nîsâbûrî
ELMALILI:50:16/r14.claim: Nisaburi defines verid as a blood-carrying vessel, unlike arteries, and veridan as the pair of vessels at the front of the neck joining the vetin.
ELMALILI:50:16/r14.anchor: Nizamüddîn Nîsâbûrî de Garâibü’l-Kur’ân nâm tefsirinde “verîd, şerâyînin gayrı olarak demi hâmil damardır

ELMALILI:50:16/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r15.claim: Habl means rope or bond and can mean vessel; most take habl al-warid as the vein, a general-to-specific construction.
ELMALILI:50:16/r15.anchor: ip ve bağ demektir. Damar mânasına

ELMALILI:50:16/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r16.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:50:16/r16.claim: Zamakhshari allows habl to mean the base of the neck, making a lāmī genitive and permitting a metaphor for neck or body.
ELMALILI:50:16/r16.anchor: Zemahşerî bu mâna ile lâmî izâfeti de tecviz eylemiştir

ELMALILI:50:16/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r17.claim: The genitive can be a simile: the vein is imagined as a rope around the neck.
ELMALILI:50:16/r17.anchor: izâfet-i teşbîhiyye ile “verîd ipi”, boyuna dolanmış ipe benzeyen verîd mefhûmunu

ELMALILI:50:16/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r18.claim: Since verid is singular but generic, the phrase may mean the whole vein network or the vena cava.
ELMALILI:50:16/r18.anchor: Verîd müfred olmak itibariyle cinse hamlolunmak lâzım geleceği cihetle

ELMALILI:50:16/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r19.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:50:16/r19.claim: Raghib takes habl al-warid to mean the spirit.
ELMALILI:50:16/r19.anchor: Râgıb, “habl-i verîd”den murad rûh olduğuna kāil olmuştur

ELMALILI:50:16/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r20.claim: The vein is apt because it gathers blood toward the heart, unlike outward-flowing arteries; the poet uses it as a proverb for nearness, meaning nearer than one’s closest vessel or life.
ELMALILI:50:16/r20.anchor: Nitekim şâir وَالْمَوْتُ أَدْنَى لَهُ مِنَ الْوَرِيدِ

ELMALILI:50:16/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16/r21.claim: The vein’s black blood returns used cells to the heart for purification, hinting at renewed creation and the afterlife discussed next.
ELMALILI:50:16/r21.anchor: kullanılmış, ölmüş hüceyreleri hâmil olan bir siyah kanın kalbe vürûdu bir tasfiye ile yeni bir halka

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r1.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r1.claim: Some Arab philologists take the nearness as God’s greater power to act upon and control the person.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r1.anchor: Bazıları bunun mânası dediler, نَحْنُ أَمْلَكُ بِهِ وَأَقـْرَبُ إلَيْهِ فِي الْمَقْدِرَةِ عَلَيْهِ

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r2.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r2.claim: Other Arab philologists understand the nearness as greater knowledge of the whisper within a person.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r2.anchor: Bazıları da nefsindeki vesveseyi bilmekte daha yakın demektir dediler.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r3.claim: Elmalılı says the reported interpreters do not mean nearness of God’s Essence; they choose nearness of power’s effect or of knowledge according to the discourse.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r3.anchor: Yani kurb-i Zât mânası anlayan olmadı, ancak kelâmın sevkine nazaran

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r4.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r4.claim: Rāzī reads the phrase as perfect divine knowledge: a vein can be screened from its owner, but nothing can screen God’s knowledge.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r4.anchor: Fahr-ı Râzî bunu şöyle ifade etmiştir: “Allah teâlâ’nın ilminin kemâlini beyandır.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r5.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r5.claim: Rāzī also offers a power reading: God’s command acts in the person as blood flows through the veins.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r5.anchor: Emrimiz onda damarlarındaki kanın cereyânı gibi cereyan eder.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r6.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashshāf calls the nearness metaphorical: God’s knowledge encompasses a person and every hidden state as though He were physically near.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r6.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf da şöyle der: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ mecazdır. Murad ona ilminin yakınlığı

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r7.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r7.claim: He compares this expression with saying God is everywhere, while affirming that God is exalted above and transcendent from places.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r7.anchor: Nitekim ‘Allah her yerdedir’ denilir, hâlbuki Allah mekânlardan ecell ve münezzehtir.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r8.claim: Elmalılı explains the metaphor because literal nearness and distance apply spatially to bodies, whereas spatial proximity cannot be conceived of God.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r8.anchor: lügatta yakınlık ve uzaklık mekân ve mesafe itibariyle cismâniyyâtta hakikat olduğu

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r9.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî ile Ebussuud
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r9.claim: They paraphrase the verse as knowing a person better than whoever is nearer to him than his jugular; essential nearness stands metaphorically for knowledge-nearness, which it causes.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r9.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî ile Ebussuud da bunu bir nükte ilâvesiyle hulâsa etmişler

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r10.claim: Elmalılı supplies an elided comparison, “than whoever is nearer to him,” because a jugular vein cannot itself be the comparator for knowledge.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r10.anchor: Görülüyor ki bu ifadede مِ َّمنْ كَانَ اَقـْرَبَ اِلَيْهِ diye bir mufaddalun aleyh takdir olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r11.claim: One possible referent of the omitted “whoever” is the person himself; the vein then stands for the person, whom God knows better than he knows himself.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r11.anchor: O ya kendisinden kinayedir, bu surette “habl-i verîd”den murad kendi şahsı olup mâna onu kendisinden daha iyi biliriz demek olur

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r12.claim: Alternatively, “whoever” means the recording angels: they are nearer to the person than his vein, while God is nearer still, as the following passage suggests.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r12.anchor: Yahut zikrolunacak meleklerdir ki bu surette o hafaza

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r13.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r13.claim: Ālūsī remarks that expressions of the people of spiritual realization are difficult for those without such spiritual states.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r13.anchor: Âlûsî burada “ehl-i vahdetin kelâmı hâl sâhibi olmayanlar için zor anlaşılır şeylerdendir” demiştir.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r14.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿArabī calls the station of the Near One the highest station, essential for those who stumble, and describes its paradox as nearness containing distance.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r14.anchor: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî’nin Futûhât-ı Mekkiyye’sinin Esmâ-i Hüsnâ bâbında “Akreb” ism-i şerîfinde şu sözlerini nakledelim: حَضْرَةُ الأَْقْرَب أَعْلَى الْحَضَرَاتِ

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r15.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r15.claim: He says the servant is called “servant of the Nearer” or “servant of the Near,” citing God’s nearness and hearing, and the report that God descends to the lower heaven.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r15.anchor: Bu hazretin sâhibine ‘abdü’l-akreb’ ve ‘abdü’l-karîb’ denilir. Çünkü O azze ve celle bize habl-i verîdden akrebdir

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r16.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r16.claim: For Ibn ʿArabī, God is with people wherever they are and nearer to them than themselves; human connection and every faculty ultimately depend on God.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r16.anchor: çünkü nerede olsak bizimle beraberdir, onun için Karîb, Akreb isimleriyle müsemmâdır. O bize bizden daha yakındır.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r17.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r17.claim: He contrasts the vein, merely a channel for life and blood, with God as the source of hearing, sight, standing, sitting, will, and judgment.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r17.anchor: Zira bizden habl-i verîdin gayesi diğer damarların hâli gibi hükm-i hayâtın mecrâsı ve kanların

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r18.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r18.claim: He says God legislated ways of nearness and made humans in His form; the servant is at once close as a counterpart and distant as an opposite.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r18.anchor: Sonra Allah teâlâ bizde de kendisine kurbu teşrî‘buyurdu. Çünkü biz O’nun sureti üzere mahlukları olduğumuz cihetle

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r19.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r19.claim: Through prescribed acts performed in humility, the servant draws near until God becomes his hearing, sight, and powers, as in the cited sacred report.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r19.anchor: yapmakla O onun sem‘i, basarı ve cemî‘-i kuvâsı olana kadar bu suretle kul

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r20.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r20.claim: He argues that the report’s pronoun still establishes the servant as himself; divine manifestation in the servant’s faculties does not mean the servant and God are identical.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r20.anchor: zamiri abde ircâ‘ile abdin aynını tesbit etmiş ve o, hüve hüve olmadığını isbat eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r21.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r21.claim: He describes the cosmos as containing no other than God manifest through the stations of His beautiful names, while God remains transcendent and beyond them.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r21.anchor: Artık kevnde başka yok ancak O, esmâ-i hüsnâsının

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r22.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r22.claim: He says the law encompasses claimants and others.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r22.anchor: şeriat müddeîye ve gayr-i müddeîye âm oldu.

ELMALILI:50:16#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r23.speaker: Şeyh Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r23.claim: He says people are resurrected according to intention and distinguished by their religion and school.
ELMALILI:50:16#2/r23.anchor: kıyamet günü niyetine göre haşrolunur ve millet ve mezhebiyle seçilir.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r1.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn ʿArabī affirms essential and active nearness, ending in the servant’s annihilation and unity; some of this discussion is difficult for spiritual outsiders.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r1.anchor: Görülüyor ki Şeyh beytinde bizzat kurba kāil olmuş ve kurb-i fiili anlatmış, sonunu da abdin fenâsıyla vahdete bağlamıştır.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r2.claim: The Prophet’s reported descent to the lower heaven should indicate nearness of command, not place; the hadith does not say descent from the Throne.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r2.anchor: Hadiste nüzul var ise de Arş’tan kaydı yoktur

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r3.claim: Elmalılı warns against turning unity of being into union: the verse opens by emphatically stating that humans are created, preserving the distinction between Creator and creature.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r3.anchor: Hâlık ve mahlûkun hakkı gözetilmek için evvelemirde وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ kasemiyle insanın mahlûkiyetini te’kîden tansis buyurmuştur.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r4.claim: Citing Ibn al-Munayyir’s Kashshāf gloss, Elmalılı states his creed: nothing exists apart from God’s essence, attributes, and acts; God makes some acts the locus of others.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r4.anchor: olmak üzere Keşşâf hâşiyesinde İbn Müneyyir’in

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r5.claim: All the world is God’s act and creation, including human acts attributed to people by compulsion or choice, as affirmed in 37:96; this is necessary monotheism for a believer.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r5.anchor: bütün âlem Allah’ın fiili, yani halkı olduğu gibi insanlar ve insanlara cebren ve ihtiyâren nisbet olunan fiiller de

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r6.claim: Attributes are neither identical with nor wholly other than the essence; acts are not their agent, and Creator and creature cannot be identical.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r6.anchor: aynı değildir, lâ-hüve velâ gayruhu’dur. Fiil de fâilin aynı olamaz. Hâlık ile mahluk hüve hüve müttehid olamaz.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r7.claim: Everything belongs to God, but belonging to God does not make it God.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r7.anchor: Allah’ın olmayan hiçbir şey yoktur, hepsi Allah’ındır, lâkin Allah’ın olmak, Allah olmak değildir.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r8.claim: Nearness preserves distinction: a messenger’s acts and strength may be attributed to the sender without making the messenger identical to the sender.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r8.anchor: resul, mürsilin aynı olmasını îcab etmez. Belki resûlün aynı sâbit olduğu hâlde kendisi de fiili de mürsilin olur.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r9.claim: A servant approaching through obligatory or supererogatory worship remains himself; divine power manifests through his faculties without making him God.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r9.anchor: kurb-i ferâizle ve gerek kurb-i nevâfille tekarrub etmiş olan abdin de aynı sâbit olmakla beraber

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r10.claim: Spatial nearness entails an interval and is therefore a kind of distance; attributing place to God would make space greater than or partly outside His encompassing.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r10.anchor: mekânî yakınlık mutlaka arada bir faslı istilzam eder, aradaki fâsılanın büyüklüğüne küçüklüğüne göre mülâhaza olunur

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r11.claim: Because God transcends place and encompasses everything, Elmalılı explains nearness through attributes rather than essence to prevent imagining spatial proximity.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r11.anchor: kurb-i mekânî tevehhüm olunmamak için kurb-i zât ile değil

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r12.claim: Because a human is embodied and occupies space, describing God as near to the person’s essence could suggest spatial proximity; the metaphor rejects spatial, not divine essential, nearness.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r12.anchor: insanın zâtı bir cism-i mütemekkin olduğundan dolayı ona kurb-i zatî ile akrebiyet mülâhazası bir kurb-i mekânî îham edebilir.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r13.claim: Since metaphor is necessary here, exegetes select the safest meaning for the general public.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r13.anchor: müfessirîn, umum için en sâlim olan mânayı ihtiyar eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r14.claim: In divine names and attributes, the intended end is their effects, such as glad tidings or warnings, even if “nearer” is read as essential nearness.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r14.anchor: sıfât ve esmâ-yı ilâhiyede matlub gāyâtı olduğuna göre akreb vasfı kurb-i zat ile tefsir edilse bile

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r15.claim: The statement that God is with people wherever they are has traditionally been explained as His knowledge; Elmalılı likewise allows knowledge or power as the sense of nearness here.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r15.anchor: ile tefsir olunduğu gibi buradaki akrebiyet de naklettiğimiz vechile ilim veya kudret yakınlığıyla tefsir olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r16.claim: Elmalılı sees contextual cues as supporting both kinds of nearness, and asks why commentators state knowledge and power disjunctively; he finds no explicit answer.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r16.anchor: Bakılırsa bunun cem‘inde münâfat olmamalı, hem ilmi hem kudreti ile akrebiyet murad olunabilmeli idi, acaba niçin terdid ile söyleniyor?

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r17.claim: One proposed reason for the disjunction is that two metaphors or their implications may not be combined; Elmalılı thinks a representative metaphor or metonymy could allow it.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r17.anchor: kurb-ı zattan mecaz olmak hasebiyle iki mecazın, iki lâzımın bir arada cem‘i tecviz edilememek

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r18.claim: A second proposed reason is that contextual cues support different senses: some indicate knowledge and others power, producing exegetical disagreement.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r18.anchor: siyak ve sibakda خَلَقْنَا، نَعْلَمُ، اِذْ يَتَلَقَّى، وَجَائَتْ، وَنُفِخَ gibi karînelerin bazısı yalnız ilmi bazısı da kudreti

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r19.claim: Elmalılı favors combining the senses: knowledge is broader but does not entail power, whereas power entails knowledge; a power reading therefore also conveys knowledge.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r19.anchor: Kudret ise ilmi müstelzimdir. Kudret ile kurb murad edildiği takdirde

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r20.claim: After explicitly stating God’s knowledge of inner whispers, the added nearness clause points beyond knowledge alone; Elmalılı understands it as also implying power, care, kindness, and wrath.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r20.anchor: Onun için biz bundan yalnız ilmen kurb değil, lutf u inâyete kahr u gazaba da darb-ı mesel olabilen bir kurb anlıyoruz ki bu lâekal kurb-i kudrettir.

ELMALILI:50:16#3/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r21.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r21.claim: Rāghib says qurb and distance are opposites used for place, time, relation, rank or honor, benefit, care, and power; his examples span the cited verses.
ELMALILI:50:16#3/r21.anchor: Râgıb Müfredât’ında der ki: “Kurb ve bu‘d mütekābildirler. Kurb zamanda, mekânda, nisbette, huzve

ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r3.claim: God is nearer to a person than the angels and knows hidden matters in the soul that even they cannot perceive, with power to act as He wills.
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r3.anchor: Allah ona her yakından daha yakındır.

ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r7.claim: The context indicates that God knows inward whispers that remain hidden from the recording angels.
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r7.anchor: Mâkabline nazaran sevkinden de nefisteki vesveseler gibi bazı şeylerin Allah’a mâlum olmakla beraber onlardan gizli kaldığı anlaşılmıştı

ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r10.claim: Passing inner thoughts that never reach intention, resolve, or decision are not written; these are unsettled self-whispers.
ELMALILI:50:17-29#2/r10.anchor: Demek ki hemm, azim, karar mertebelerine gelmeyen vesveseler yazılmaz, bu cihetle مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ hemm ve kasd mertebesine gelmeyen ehâdîs-i nefs

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:16/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:16/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:16/r7.claim: While the angels record, God is already nearer to each person than the person is to himself and knows everything.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:50:16/r7.anchor: insana kendinden daha yakın olan Allah zaten her şeyi bilmektedir.

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r1.claim: In the poetic phrase 'you command the heart to act,' the verb means 'you command me'; Bāqillānī rejects the metaphor because a heart cannot be commanded.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r1.anchor: ثم قوله تأمري القلب يفعل معناه تأمريني والقلب لا يؤمر

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r2.claim: One gloss takes 'my garments' for the body, by analogy with the Qur'anic phrase about purifying one's garments.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r2.anchor: ذكر الثوب وأراد البدن مثل قول الله تعالى ( ﴿ وثيابك فطهر ﴾ )

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses the garment image as separation or abandonment and says tansal means to part.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة هذا مثل للهجر وتنسل تبين

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r4.claim: Bāqillānī calls the first line weak and low: its self-deprecating description would justify abandonment, yet the poet presents himself as refined and deserving continued attachment.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r4.anchor: وهو بيت قليل المعنى ركيكه ووضيعه

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r5.claim: The second hemistich has an unusual but modest and intimate metaphor.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r5.anchor: والاستعارة في المصرع الثاني فيها تواضع وتقارب وإن كانت غريبة

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī explains 'aʿshār' as a heart broken into pieces, like a vessel called aʿshār when shattered; Bāqillānī considers this the more likely interpretation.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r6.anchor: هذا تأويل ذكره الأصمعي وهو أشبه عند أكثرهم

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r7.speaker: غيره
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes the two eyes as the al-muʿallā and al-raqīb arrows, worth seven and three shares in the camel division, meaning she has taken his whole heart.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r7.anchor: وقال غيره وهذا مثل للأعشار التي تقسم الجزور عليها

BAQILLANI:v1p169/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r8.claim: The arrow reading avoids an awkward phrase but spoils the meaning: if the lover's whole heart already belongs to her, her weeping cannot make it wholly hers.
BAQILLANI:v1p169/r8.anchor: ولكن من حمل على التأويل الثاني سلم من الخلل الواقع في اللفظ ولكنه يفسد المعنى ويختل

BURHAN:v4p443/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p443/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p443/r8.claim: يا normally addresses someone distant, as in calling God despite His nearness; this reflects the caller's humility and sense of remoteness from divine favor.
BURHAN:v4p443/r8.anchor: ومنه قول الداعي يا الله وهو

QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r10.claim: The soul whispers desires to satisfy itself, including affectation before people, bad character, rancor, and other afflictions that disturb the heart and its time.
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r10.anchor: نعلم ما توسوس به نفسه من شهوات تطلب استنفاذها ، مثل التصنع مع الخلق ، وسوء الخلق ، والحقد

QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r11.claim: The vein is the nearest part of a person to himself; the verse means God's knowledge and power, His hearing of speech, and that no affair is unclear to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r11.anchor: فحبل الوريد أقرب أجزاء نفسه إلى نفسه ، والمراد من ذلك العلم والقدرة ، وأنه يسمع قولهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r12.claim: This verse brings awe, panic, and fear to some, but spirit, tranquility, and intimacy of heart to others.
QUSHAYRI:v3p226/r12.anchor: وفي هذه الآية هيبة وفزع وخوف لقوم ، وروح وسكون وأنس قلب لقوم

ITQAN:v3p19/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p19/r3.claim: The divine nearness in both verses is interpreted as nearness by knowledge.
ITQAN:v3p19/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك صفة القرب في قوله ﴿ فإني قريب ﴾ ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد ﴾ أي بالعلم

ITQAN:v3p19/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p19/r12.claim: The general rule is that an attribute whose literal reality is impossible for God is interpreted through its necessary implication.
ITQAN:v3p19/r12.anchor: وقد قال العلماء كل صفة يستحيل حقيقتها على الله تعالى تفسر بلازمها

ITQAN:v3p19/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r13.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
ITQAN:v3p19/r13.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi says psychological states have an onset and an outcome: divine anger means intending harm, not bodily agitation, and divine shyness means refraining, not inward shrinking.
ITQAN:v3p19/r13.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين جميع الأعراض النفسانية أعني الرحمة والفرح والسرور والغضب والحياء والمكر والاستهزاء لها أوائل ولها غايات

SULAMI:v2p266#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r1.claim: Some travel with God without recourse, seeking, or flight, since God reaches them, is with them, knows their inner thoughts, and witnesses their outward movements.
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r1.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز : هم قوم ساروا مع الله بلا سبب ولا طلب ولا هرب لأنه مدركهم وهو معهم

SULAMI:v2p266#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r2.claim: God is more entitled and nearer to a person: He gathered him after separation, brought him into being after nonexistence, and breathed spirit into him; the nearest is the one who knows him better than he knows himself.
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : أي نحن أولى به واحق لأنا جمعناه بعد الافتراق وأنشأناه بعد العدم

SULAMI:v2p266#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r3.claim: Through God one knows oneself and one’s spirit; this disclosure of divine attributes is proportioned to human capacity, while no one can bear hearing the ultimate Reality.
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r3.anchor: قال أيضا في هذه الآية : به عرفت نفسك وبه عرفت روحك كان ذلك إظهار النعوت على قدر طاقة الخلق

SULAMI:v2p266#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r4.claim: A servant who inwardly witnesses God’s nearness draws near through obedience and gathers his concern before God by constant remembrance in public and private.
SULAMI:v2p266#5/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : القرب لعبد شاهد بقلبه قرب الله منه فتقرب إلى الله بطاعته وجمع همه

ITQAN:v2p330#6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p330#6/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p330#6/r5.claim: The hab al-warid is the vein of the neck.
ITQAN:v2p330#6/r5.anchor: 1967 ﴿ من حبل الوريد ﴾ الوريد عرق العنق

DAMGHANI:v1p462/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r1.claim: Nafs can mean the heart; the source also glosses what is within a person in al-Isrāʾ as the heart.
DAMGHANI:v1p462/r1.anchor: وقال تعالى في سورة ق ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه

DAMGHANI:v1p49/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r2.claim: In another usage, al-insān refers to Adam’s descendants, as in the verses about the self’s whispering and creation from a mixed drop.
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r2.anchor: الإنسان ولد آدم . قوله تعالى في سورة ق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r1.claim: Al-insān is singular, with nās and anāsī as plurals, and indeclinable in the source’s account.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r1.anchor: الإنسان : واحد الناس ، والجمع : ناس وأناسي ، ولا يصرف .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r2.claim: One proposed etymology connects insān with intimacy, because a person feels familiar with their own kind.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : سمي إنسان : لأنه يأنس بجنسه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives ins from visibility and the eye’s ability to perceive people, connecting it with anastu, “I saw.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : سمي الإنس إنسا ، لظهورهم ، وإدراك البصر [ إياهم ] . وهو من قولك : آنست كذا ، أي : أبصرته .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly says humans were named for being entrusted with a covenant and then forgetting it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r4.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال : إنما سمي الإنسان إنسانا لأنه عهد إليه فنسي .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r5.speaker: قوم من المفسرين من أهل اللغة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r5.claim: Some linguist exegetes support the forgetfulness derivation through the diminutive unaysiyān, restoring a form whose yāʾ was dropped for ease.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r5.anchor: وذهب إلى هذا قوم من المفسرين من أهل اللغة واحتجوا في ذلك بتصغير إنسان وذلك : أن العرب تصغره على ' أنيسيان ' : بزيادة ياء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r6.speaker: البصريون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r6.claim: Basran grammarians analyze insān as faʿlān on the visibility derivation; its diminutive adds yāʾ as in layla to layila.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r6.anchor: والبصريون ( 27 / أ ) يجعلونه ' فعلان ' على التفسير الأول .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r7.claim: Exegetes are said to give al-insān twenty-five Qurʾanic referents; this passage gives Adam, humankind, and Abū Bakr as examples.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الإنسان في القرآن على خمسة وعشرين وجها : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r8.claim: Al-insān can refer to Adam, in descriptions of creation from clay and a time before he was remembered.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r8.anchor: أحدها : آدم [ عليه السلام ] . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين : ﴿ ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r9.claim: Al-insān can refer to Adam’s descendants or humankind generally, including verses about inner whispering, creation, deeds, and human creation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r9.anchor: والثاني : أولاد آدم . ومنه قوله تعالى في ق : ﴿ ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r10.claim: In the verse about care for parents, al-insān refers specifically to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq; the passage says it was revealed about him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p176#2/r10.anchor: والثالث : أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحقاف :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r1.claim: In ordinary usage, ḥabl is something twisted from fiber, cotton, wool, or similar material.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r1.anchor: الحبل في التعارف [ هو ] : المفتول من الليف ، أو القطن ، أو الصوف ، أو نحو ذلك .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r2.claim: A covenant is called a rope because holding to it reaches one’s goal; the cited line uses ḥabl for such a bond.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r2.anchor: ويقال للعهد : حبل ، لأن المتمسك به يصل إلى مطلوبه ، وأنشدوا : - فلو حبلا تناول من سليمي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r3.speaker: الأعشى
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r3.claim: Aman, security or safe-conduct, is called a rope because it extends safety and a route to one’s destination; al-Aʿshā uses ḥibāl for guarantees.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r3.anchor: ويقال للأمان : حبل لأن الأمن منبسط بالأمان فهو حبل له إلى كل موضع يريده قال الأعشى : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r4.claim: One Qurʾanic sense is an ordinary rope, as in the magicians’ ropes and Abū Lahab’s wife’s palm-fiber rope.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r4.anchor: أحدها : الحبل المتعارف ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء : ﴿ فألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r5.claim: A second sense is a covenant, as in the covenant with God and with people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r5.anchor: والثاني : العهد ، ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران : ﴿ إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس ﴾ ، أي : بعهد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r6.claim: A third sense is the vein in the neck, the meaning of ḥabl al-warīd in this verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r6.anchor: والثالث : عرق في العنق ، ومنه قوله تعالى في قاف : ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r7.claim: A fourth sense is the Qurʾan, which believers are told to hold fast to together.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p241/r7.anchor: والرابع : القرآن ، ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران : ﴿ واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ﴾

FARRA:v3p77/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p77/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p77/r1.claim: The pronoun in به can refer to ما; alternatively ما refers to the person, with the pronoun meaning the one to whom the self whispers and speaks.
FARRA:v3p77/r1.anchor: وقد يكون ما توسوس أن تجعل الهاء للرجل الذي توسوس به

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r1.claim: The two warīds are veins between the throat and the two upper chest or shoulder joints.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r2.claim: The ḥabl is the warīd itself, described by two names; the construction is a genitive annexation to itself because the names differ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p418#3/r2.anchor: والحبل هو: الوريد؛ فأضيف إلى نفسه: لاختلاف لفظي اسميه (3) .

NAHHAS:v4p223/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p223/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p223/r7.claim: The pronoun in به refers to ما.
NAHHAS:v4p223/r7.anchor: الضمير الذي في به يعود على ما

NAHHAS:v4p223/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p223/r8.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p223/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows the pronoun to refer instead to الإنسان.
NAHHAS:v4p223/r8.anchor: وأجاز الفراء أن يعود على الإنسان أي ويعلم ما توسوس إليه نفسه

NAHHAS:v4p223/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p223/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p223/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the wārid as the cord of the neck.
NAHHAS:v4p223/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس الوريد حبل العنق

NAHHAS:v4p223/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p223/r10.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v4p223/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash Saʿīd says God is nearer to the person by power than the jugular vein.
NAHHAS:v4p223/r10.anchor: قال الأخفش سعيد ونحن أقرب إليه بالمقدرة من حبل الوريد

NAHHAS:v4p223/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p223/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p223/r11.claim: Another view says God is nearer in knowledge of the soul’s whispers than the jugular vein.
NAHHAS:v4p223/r11.anchor: وقال غيره أي ونحن أقرب إليه في العلم بما توسوس به نفسه من حبل الوريد

SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r1.claim: ونعلم is the predicate of an omitted subject, ونحن نعلم; the resulting nominal clause is circumstantial. It cannot itself be a circumstantial clause because it is a positive imperfect directly joined to wāw; the same applies to ونحن أقرب.
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r1.anchor: قوله: { ونعلم }: خبر مبتدأ مضمر. تقديره: ونحن نعلم. والجملة الاسمية حينئذ حال.

SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r2.claim: The idafa may mean the cord belonging to the vein, like مسجد الجامع; clarify the broad word حبل, like بعير سانية; or refer to the neck cord added to the vein because both are in one organ.
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r2.anchor: هذا كقولهم: مسجد الجامع أي: حبل العرق الوريد، أو لأن الحبل أعم للبيان نحو: بعير سانية،

SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r3.claim: الوريد may mean the arriving vessel or the one arrived at; it is a large neck vein, said to be two.
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r3.anchor: والوريد: إما بمعنى الوارد، وإما بمعنى المورود. والوريد: عرق كبير في العنق يقال: إنهما وريدان.

SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari describes two veins flanking the front of the neck and connecting to the aorta; their name reflects the spirit arriving there from the head.
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " عرقان مكتنفان لصفحتي العنق في مقدمهما يتصلان بالوتين،

SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r5.claim: An unattributed poem compares the two veins to a hide rope.

SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r6.speaker: الأثرم
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r6.claim: Al-Athram calls the wateen the body's river in the heart, the abhar in the back, akhal and nisa in arm and thigh, and aslam in the little finger.
SAMIN-DURR:50:16/r6.anchor: وقال الأثرم: " هو نهر الجسد: هو في القلب الوتين، وفي الظهر الأبهر،

ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r4.claim: God knows what a person conceals and keeps within himself.
ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r4.anchor: أي نعلم ما يخفي وما يكنه في نفسه

ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r5.claim: Al-warīd is a vein inside the neck, and there are two; an unnamed poet's use of the dual وريداه supports this, with رشاء explained as fiber.
ZAJJAJ:v5p43#2/r5.anchor: والوريد عرق في باطن العنق، وهما وريدان، قال الشاعر. كأن وريداه رشاءا خلب يعني من ليف

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r1.claim: What the self whispers is what it says to a person or what comes to mind; waswasa is a faint sound like jewelry rustling.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r1.anchor: أي ما تحدثه به وهو ما يخطر بالبال والوسوسة الصوت الخفي ومنه وسواس الحلي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to relative ma and the preposition attaches to tawaswasa; accompaniment or redundancy is possible but weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r2.anchor: وجوز أن تكون للملابسة أو زائدة وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r3.claim: Alternatively, ma is a verbal noun and the pronoun refers to the human; the preposition makes the soul's whispering affect him.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ( ما ) مصدرية والضمير للأنسان والباء للتعدية

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r4.speaker: لبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r4.claim: Labid's verse about contradicting the speaking self illustrates the idiom.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r4.anchor: قال لبيد : وأكذب النفس إذا حدثتها إن صدق النفس يزري بالأمل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r5.claim: God's nearness means complete knowledge, not spatial proximity, since God transcends place.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r5.anchor: أي نعلم به وبأحواله لا يخفى علينا شيء من خفياته على أنه أطلق السبب وأريد المسبب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r6.claim: The wording is an analogy for God's closeness in knowledge; unity-language from people of spiritual states is difficult for others.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r6.anchor: أو الكلام من باب التمثيل ولا مجال لحمله على القرب المكاني لتنزهه سبحانه عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r7.claim: The jugular-rope image expresses extreme closeness, like the midwife's seat idiom.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r7.anchor: و ( حبل الوريد ) مثل في فرط القرب كقولهم : مقعد القابلة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r8.speaker: ذو الرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r8.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses the jugular rope as an image of nearness.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r8.anchor: قال ذو الرمة على ما في الكشاف : والموتأدنى لي من حبل الوريد

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r9.claim: Habl means rope but here denotes the vein by resemblance; its annexation to warid clarifies or specifies.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r9.anchor: والحبل معروف والمراد به هنا العرق لشبهه به وإضافته إلى الوريد وهو عرق مخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r10.speaker: الأثرم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r10.claim: Al-Athram calls warid the river of the body; the source names veins in heart, back, limbs, and little finger.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r10.anchor: وعن الأثرم أنه نهر الجسد ويقال له في العنق الوريد وفي القلب الوتين

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r11.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r11.claim: Al-Kashshaf describes two veins flanking the front neck and connected to the watin.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r11.anchor: ففي الكشاف الوريد أن عرقان مكتنفان لصفحتي العنق في مقدمها متصلان بالوتين

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r12.claim: Warid may be an active or passive participle because animal spirit reaches the vein.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r12.anchor: فالوريد فعيل بمعنى فاعل وقيل : هو بمعنى مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r13.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r13.claim: Al-Raghib describes warid as a vein linking liver and heart through which spirit flows; some say God is nearer than a person's spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p178/r13.anchor: قول الراغب : الوريد عرق متصل بالكبد والقلب وفيه مجري الروح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.claim: God knows what a person's heart whispers and is aware of hidden thoughts and secrets.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r4.anchor: يحدث به قلبه ولا يخفى علينا سرائره وضمائره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.claim: God's nearness means His greater knowledge; bodily parts conceal one another, but nothing conceals anything from His knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r5.anchor: أعلم به، {من حبل الوريد} لأن أبعاضه وأجزاءه يحجب بعضها بعضا، ولا يحجب علم الله شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
