BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.claim: The hablu al-warid is the neck vein between the throat and the two al-albawain, branching throughout the body.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r6.anchor: عرق العنق، وهو عرق بين الحلقوم والعلباوين، يتفرق في البدن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.claim: Habl is itself the vein; the genitive construction joins two expressions differing in wording.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p358#2/r7.anchor: والحبل هو الوريد، فأضيف إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.claim: Independent forms such as أنت and هو can follow attached pronouns in the same case, as in مررت بك أنت and رأيتك أنت.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.anchor: اعلم أن هذه الحروف كلها تكون وصفا للمجرور والمرفوع والمنصوب المضمرين

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.claim: These pronoun forms are not ordinary adjectives like الطويل; they behave more like نفسه, preserving the grammatical role of the pronoun they accompany.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.anchor: ولكنه بمنزلة نفسه إذا قلت مررت به نفسه

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.claim: Pronouns do not describe overt nouns, since that would make an overt noun take a pronominal modifier; this parallels rejecting أجمعون or نفسه after an indefinite noun.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الحروف لا تكون وصفا للمظهر كراهية أن

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.claim: A pronoun may be replaced by an appositional pronoun: use إياك or إياه for the accusative and أنت or هو for the nominative.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.anchor: فأنت وهو وأخواتهما نظائر إياه في النصب

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.claim: A pronoun can be apposition to an overt noun but not its adjective; apposition is independent, as if the noun were repeated in a new clause.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.anchor: رأيت زيدا ثم قلت إياه رأيت

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.claim: The mixed phrase مررت به وبزيد هما is awkward; if intended as apposition, repeat the preposition and say مررت به وبزيد بهما.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهذهالحروفكلهاتكونوصفاللمج.anchor: واعلم أنه قبيح أن تقول مررت به وبزيد هما كما قبح أن

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r8.claim: What the soul whispers is what it inwardly speaks to a person: whatever occurs to the mind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r8.anchor: ما تحدثه به نفسه وهو ما يخطر بالبال

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r9.claim: Waswasa is a faint, hidden sound; the word is also used for the tinkling of jewelry.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r9.anchor: والوسوسة الصوت الخفي ومنها وسواس الحلي

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r10.claim: If mā is relative, the pronoun refers back to it and the bāʾ works as in the expression ‘a sound in something.’
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r10.anchor: والضمير لما إن جعلت موصولة والباء مثلها في صوت بكذا

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r11.claim: Alternatively, if mā is a verbal noun, the pronoun refers to the human and the bāʾ makes the verb transitive.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r12.claim: God is nearer than the jugular vein in knowledge of the person's condition, nearer than anyone physically close to him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r12.anchor: أي ونحن أعلم بحاله ممن كان أقرب إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r13.claim: Closeness of essence is a figure for closeness of knowledge; the jugular is a proverbial image of nearness, as the poetic line says death is nearer than the vein.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r13.anchor: تجوز بقرب الذات لقرب العلم لأنه موجبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r14.claim: Ḥabl means a vein or cord and is a clarifying annexation; the two jugular veins flank the front sides of the neck and connect by the watīn toward the head.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r15.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r15.claim: One reported etymology says the vein is called warīd because the spirit goes to it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:14-16/r15.anchor: وقيل سمي وريدا لأن الروح ترده

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r7.claim: Humanity is an especially wondrous, comprehensive creation, combining intimacy and arrogance, memory and forgetfulness, ignorance and knowledge, obedience and disobedience; God appoints guardians over every state.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r7.anchor: وهو أعجب خلقا وأجمع من جميع ما مضى ذكره بما فيه من الأنس والطغيان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r8.claim: God knows hidden thoughts now and in the future, even before they emerge from the unseen into the soul’s secret store; a person may not control them himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r8.anchor: الآن وفيما بعد ذلك مما لم ينقدح بعد من خزائن الغيب إلى سر النفس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r9.claim: The deniers’ hearts know God’s power, the Qur’an’s truth and inimitability, and the Messenger’s veracity; envy, rivalry, pride, and ambition drive their habitual verbal denial.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r9.anchor: أن قلوبهم عالمة بقدرتنا على أكمل ما نريد وبصحة القرآن وإعجازه وصدق الرسول به صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r10.claim: God’s nearness here is nearness of knowledge and witness, without spatial distance; unlike bodily parts, nothing can screen anything from His knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r10.anchor: قرب علم وشهود من غير مسافة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r11.claim: The expression is generic: the two jugular veins lie like ropes along the front sides of the neck, extending from the head to the heart’s great vein.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r11.anchor: والوريدان عرقان كالحبلين مكتنفان لصفحتي العنق في مقدمها متصلات من الرأس إلى الوتين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r12.claim: The jugular is an image of extreme closeness, and the annexation follows the pattern of the expression مسجد الجامع.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r13.claim: The author points back to his useful discussion of the same divine protection in al-Māʾida.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r13.anchor: وقد مضى في تفسري سورة المائدة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r14.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r14.claim: Al-Qushayri says the verse brings awe, alarm, and fear to some, but spiritual life, intimacy, and settled hearts to others.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p254/r14.anchor: قال القشيري : وفي هذه الآية هيبة وفزع وخوف لقوم

DURR-FULL:v7p592/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r2.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r2.claim: A report from Abū Saʿīd says God is nearer to Adam's descendant than the jugular vein, intervenes between person and heart, holds every creature by its forelock, and is with people wherever they are.
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: نزل الله من ابن آدم أرفع المنازل

DURR-FULL:v7p592/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r3.claim: Asked about God's nearness, al-Ḍaḥḥāk says nothing is nearer to a person than the jugular vein, yet God is nearer than it.
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r3.anchor: عن جويبر رضي الله عنه قال: سألت الضحاك عن قوله {ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد} قال: ليس شيء أقرب إلى ابن آدم

DURR-FULL:v7p592/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the jugular cord as the vein of the neck.
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {من حبل الوريد} قال: عرق العنق

DURR-FULL:v7p592/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r5.claim: Another gloss from Ibn ʿAbbās calls it the heart's vital cord and what it carries.
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {من حبل الوريد} قال: نياط القلب وما حمل

DURR-FULL:v7p592/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the jugular cord is what lies in the throat.
DURR-FULL:v7p592/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {من حبل الوريد} قال: الذي في الحلق

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3308#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3308#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3308#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the “jugular cord” as the neck vein.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3308#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : من حبل الوريد قال : عرق العنق .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r4.claim: The verse details the first creation by focusing on humans, the most relevant creation here, then adds knowledge of inner whispers to complete 50:4 and lead to recording deeds from 50:17 onward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r4.anchor: هذا تفصيل لبعض الخلق الأول بذكر خلق الإنسان وهو أهم في هذا المقام للتنبيه على أنه المراد من الخلق الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r6.claim: The emphatic lām and qad also anticipate the coordinated clause about knowing whispers: people know God created them but do not know that He knows all their states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r6.anchor: وتأكيد هذا الخبر باللام و ( قد ) مراعى فيه المتعاطفات وهي { نعلم ما توسوس به نفسه } لأنهم وإن كانوا يعلمون أن الله خلق الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r7.claim: Al-insān includes all people, but the polytheists are its immediate target because they are the addressees; the surrounding verses make the warning clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r7.anchor: و { الإنسان } يعم جميع الناس ولكن المقصود منهم أولا المشركون لأنهم المسوق إليهم هذا الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r8.claim: The bāʾ is extra to intensify attachment, and the relative pronoun refers to what the soul speaks, as in 5:6.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r8.anchor: والباء في قوله { به } زائدة لتأكيد اللصوق ، والضمير عائد الصلة كأنه قيل : ما تتكلمه نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r9.claim: God's knowledge of each person's inner speech shows how vast His knowledge is: if He knows hidden thoughts, it is no surprise He knows what the earth removes from the dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r9.anchor: وفائدة الإخبار بأن الله يعلم ما توسوس به نفس كل إنسان التنبيه عل سعة علم الله تعالى بأحوالهم كلها فإذا كان يعلم حديث النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r10.claim: Creation is expressed in the past, but knowledge of whispering in the present to show its continuously renewed, unlimited attachment and warn against hidden intentions displeasing to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p298/r10.anchor: وأما الإخبار عن علم ما توسوس به النفس بصيغة المضارع فللدلالة على أن تعلق علمه تعالى بالوسوسة متجدد غير منقض ولا محدود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r1.claim: The clause ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد is a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in ونعلم.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r1.anchor: وجملة { ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد } في موضع الحال من ضمير { ونعلم } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r2.claim: The clause reinforces its governing statement and confirms God's continuous knowledge of a person's inner being.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r2.anchor: والمقصود منها تأكيد عاملها وتحقيق استمرار العلم بباطن الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r3.claim: Tawwaswasa means to speak softly in a whisper.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r3.anchor: ومعنى { توسوس } تتكلم كلاما خفيا همسا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r4.claim: The verbal nouns waswās and waswasa are metaphorically used for thoughts, estimates, and intentions because whispering best resembles their varied, inward states; other terms capture only some of them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r4.anchor: ومصدره الوسواس والوسوسة أطلقت هنا مجازا على ما يجول في النفس من الخواطر والتقديرات والعزائم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r5.claim: Ḥabl refers to a body cord, the thick vessels medically known as arteries, which carry blood from the heart to major organs and have names according to destination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r5.anchor: والحبل : هنا واحد حبال الجسم . وهي العروق الغليظة المعروفة في الطب بالشرايين ، واحدها : شريان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r6.claim: The author identifies the warīd as an artery emerging from the heart's left chamber, calls it the aorta in medical terminology, and describes its branches, including the carotids.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r6.anchor: والوريد : واحد من الشرايين وهو ثاني شريانين يخرجان من التجويف الأيسر من القلب . واسمه في علم الطلب أورطي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r7.claim: The vessels have different names by bodily location: warīd in the neck, watīn at the heart, abhar in the back, akḥal and nasā in arm and thigh, and aslam in the little finger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r7.anchor: وقد تختلف أسماء أجزائه باختلاف مواقعها من الجسد فهو في العنق يسمى الوريد ، وفي القلب يسمى الوتين ، وفي الظهر يسمى الأبهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r8.claim: The genitive construction is explanatory: ḥabl is the warīd, like shajar al-arāk, where a general noun is annexed to a specific one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p300/r8.anchor: وإضافة { حبل } إلى { الوريد } بيانية ، أي الحبل الذي هو الوريد ، فإن إضافة الأعم إلى الأخص إذا وقعت في الكلام كانت إضافة بيانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r1.claim: Closeness means comprehensive knowledge of a person's condition, not spatial proximity; it forms a concise simile comparing an intelligible idea with a perceptible one, built on metonymy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r1.anchor: والقرب هنا كناية عن إحاطة العلم بالحال لأن القرب يستلزم الإطلاع ، وليس هو قربا بالمكان بقرينة المشاهدة فآل الكلام إلى التشبيه البليغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r2.claim: The jugular is physically near yet unnoticed because hidden; likewise God's nearness through knowledge is unseen, making this image especially apt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r2.anchor: ومن لطائف هذا التمثيل أن حبل الوريد مع قربه لا يشعر الإنسان بقربه لخفائه ، وكذلك قرب الله من الإنسان بعلمه قرب لا يشعر به الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r3.claim: He judges this image of nearness superior to familiar comparisons such as a midwife's seat or a belt's fastening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r3.anchor: وبذلك فاق هذا التشبيه لحالة القرب كل تشبيه من نوعه ورد في كلام البلغاء . مثل قولهم : هو منه مقعد القابلة ومعقد الإزار ، وقول زهير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r4.speaker: زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r4.claim: Zuhayr's line comparing Wādī al-Rass and its people to a hand near the mouth is cited as another image of closeness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r4.anchor: وقول زهير : فهن ووادي الرس كاليد للفم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r5.speaker: حنظلة بن ثعلبة بن سيار العجلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r5.claim: Hanzala al-Ajlī's verse says death is closer to a person than his sandal strap, another poetic comparison for nearness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p301/r5.anchor:
وقول حنظلة بن سيار وهو حنظلة بن ثعلبة بن سيار العجلي مخضرم :
كل امرىء مصبح في أهله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r1.claim: These verses establish arguments against unbelievers who deny resurrection and requital.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r1.anchor: هذه آيات فيها إقامة حجج على الكفار في إنكارهم البعث والجزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r2.claim: Creation means bringing a thing into existence in an ordered, measured, wise arrangement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r2.anchor: والخلق: إنشاء الشيء على ترتيب وتقدير حكمي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r3.claim: Al-insan is a generic term for humanity.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r4.claim: Some commentators identify the human here specifically as Adam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين الإنسان هنا آدم عليه السلام وتوسوس معناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r5.claim: Waswasa means speaking within one’s thought; jewelry’s faint sound is called waswas because it is subtle, and the word is used for what is not good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r5.anchor: وتوسوس معناه: تتحدث في فكرتها، وسمي صوت الحلي وسواسا لخفائه، والوسوسة إنما تستعمل في غير الخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r6.claim: God’s nearness means His power, dominion, and grasp over the servant, with His knowledge encompassing all; it is not bodily proximity, since bodies are veiled from one another and the heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r6.anchor: عبارة عن قدرة الله على العبد، وكون العبد في قبضة القدرة، والعلم قد أحيط به، فالقرب هو بالقدرة والسلطان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r7.claim: The warid is a large neck vein, said to be two veins on the right and left.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r7.anchor: و: الوريد عرق كبير في العنق، يقال: إنهما وريدان عن يمين وشمال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ defines the warid as the part between the throat and the two al-ʿalbabayn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: هو ما بين الحلقوم والعلباوين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the warid as the watin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r10.speaker: الأثرم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r10.claim: Al-Athram describes the body’s main veins by location: watin in the heart, abhar in the back, akhal and nasa in arm and thigh, and sulaym in the little finger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r10.anchor: قال الأثرم: هو نهر الجسد هو في القلب الوتين، وفي الظهر الأبهر، وفي الذراع والفخذ: الأكحل والنسا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r11.claim: Ḥabl is a shared term specified by its genitive relation to warid, like a genus related to its kind, not a thing added to itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p159#2/r11.anchor: اسم مشترك فخصصه بالإضافة إلى الوريد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r1.claim: The human being here means Adam’s descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r1.anchor: ﴿ ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ﴾ يعني ابن آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r2.claim: The phrase means what a person’s own soul whispers or tells him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r2.anchor: أي ما تحدثه به نفسه وقال الزجاج نعلم ما يكنه في نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r3.claim: He explains the whisper as what a person keeps concealed within himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج نعلم ما يكنه في نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r4.claim: The ‘cord’ is itself the jugular vein; the genitive construction is like the previously discussed expression ‘grain of the harvest.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r4.anchor: الحبل هو الوريد وإنما أضافه إلى نفسه لما شرحناه آنفا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r5.speaker: العراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r5.claim: He describes the warīd as a vein between the throat and the two ʿalbaʾān, and also as a vein between the upper chest and those tendons.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r5.anchor: قال العراء والوريد عرق بين الحلقوم والعباوين وعنه أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj locates the warīd as a vein inside the neck; there are two of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج الوريد عرق في باطن العنق وهما وريدان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r7.claim: The ʿalbaʾān are the two yellow tendons at the back of the neck, while the labbatān are where an earring hangs near the earlobe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r7.anchor: والعلباوان العصبتان الصفراوان في متن العنق واللبتان مجرى القرط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r8.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r8.claim: Some scholars say the warīd is a vein dispersed through the body and interwoven with all its organs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r8.anchor: حكى بعض العلماء أن الوريد عرق متفرق في البدن مخالط لجميع الأعضاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r9.claim: Although parts of a person screen other parts from one another, nothing screens God’s knowledge; this explains the stated nearness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r9.anchor: فلما كانت أبعاض الإنسان يحجب بعضها بعضها أعلم أن علمه لا يحجبه شيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r10.claim: God is nearer to the person in knowledge when the two receiving angels attend him; they are the angels assigned to each human and receive his knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p9/r10.anchor: ونحن أقرب إليه حين يتلقى المتلقيان وهما الملكان الموكلان بابن آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r1.claim: God created the human and knows all his affairs, including the good and evil that his soul whispers inwardly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r1.anchor: يعلم ما توسوس به نفوس بني آدم من الخير والشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r2.claim: A sound report from the Prophet says God pardons what the Muslim community’s souls whisper, provided people neither say it nor act on it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r2.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "إن الله (1) تجاوز لأمتي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r3.claim: The nearer ones are God’s angels, not God indwelling a person; interpreting the phrase as mere knowledge avoids indwelling or union, but Ibn Kathir says the wording does not require that reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r3.anchor: يعني: ملائكته تعالى أقرب إلى الإنسان من حبل وريده (3) إليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir compares this to God being nearer to the dying person than those present, while unseen, which he explains as the nearness of the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r4.anchor: ونحن أقرب إليه منكم ولكن لا تبصرون} [الواقعة: 85] ، يعني ملائكته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r5.claim: He also compares the wording to God’s statement that “We” sent down the Reminder: angels brought the Qur’an by God’s permission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r5.anchor: فالملائكة نزلت بالذكر -وهو القرآن-بإذن الله، عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r6.claim: God enables angels to be nearer to a person than his jugular vein; a person receives an angelic prompting as well as a satanic one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r6.anchor: الملائكة أقرب إلى الإنسان من حبل وريده إليه بإقدار (6) الله لهم على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r7.claim: The Prophet also described Satan as moving through the son of Adam like blood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p398/r7.anchor: الشيطان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r1.claim: Waswasa is abundant indistinct inner talk spoken secretly; Ru'ba's verse uses the root in a prayerful context.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r1.anchor: الوسوسة كثرة حديث النفس بما لا يتحصل في حفاء وإسرار , ومنه قول رؤبة : وسوس يدعو مخلصا رب الفلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r2.speaker: الحسن والأصم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Asamm identify the vein as a cord attached to the heart; al-Asamm calls it the wateen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r2.anchor: حبل معلق به القلب , قاله الحسن . والأصم وهو الوتين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda says the vein is a vessel in the throat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنه عرق في الحلق , قاله أبو عبيدة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is a neck vein called the ḥabl al-ʿātiq; there are two, right and left.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r4.anchor: الثالث : ما قاله ابن عباس , عرق العنق ويسمى حبل العاتق , وهما وريدان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r5.claim: One reading means God is nearer to the person than the person's own jugular vein.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r5.anchor: أحدهما : ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل وريده الذي هو منه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r6.claim: Another means God has greater control over the person than his jugular vein does.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r6.anchor: الثاني : ونحن أملك به من حبل وريده , مع استيلائه عليه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r7.claim: God's knowledge of inner whispers is closer than the heart's knowledge, though the vein is intertwined with the heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p346/r7.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : ونحن أعلم بما توسوس به نفسه من حبل وريده

MUJAHID:v2p610#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p610#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p610#4/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the jugular vein here as the one in the throat.
MUJAHID:v2p610#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد ﴾ يعني الذي في الحلق

MUQATIL:50:16/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:16/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:16/r1.claim: The self that whispers is the heart.
MUQATIL:50:16/r1.anchor: { ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه } يعني قلبه

MUQATIL:50:16/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:16/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:16/r2.claim: God's knowledge is nearer to the heart than the vein mixed with it.
MUQATIL:50:16/r2.anchor: وهو عرق خالط القلب فعلم الرب تعالى أقرب إلى القلب من ذلك العرق

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r1.claim: Waswasa is a quiet sound; the soul's whispering is what occurs to a person's mind or stirs in the heart as inward speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r1.anchor: الوسوسة الصوت الخفى ووسوسة النفس ما يخطر ببال الانسان ويهجس في ضميره من حديث النفس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r2.claim: The bāʾ has the same usage as in the expression “a sound about such-and-such.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r2.anchor: والباء مثلها في قوله صوت بكذا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r3.claim: Allah's being nearer to the person means the nearness of His knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r3.anchor: ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه ﴾ المراد قرب علمه منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r4.claim: The jugular is a vein inside the neck; ḥabl means vein, and the genitive construction explains the first noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p171#7/r4.anchor: ﴿ من حبل الوريد ﴾ هو مثل في فرط القر والوريد عرق في باطن العنق

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولقد خلقنا الإنسان } يعني الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r2.claim: An unnamed alternative identifies al-insān as Adam.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r3.claim: On the Adam reading, the whisper was to eat from the tree; the statement then generalizes to Adam’s descendants.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r3.anchor: فالذي وسوست به نفسه هو الأكل من الشجرة، ثم هو عام لولده

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r4.claim: The verse encompasses hidden stirrings in the secret, heart, and conscience, warning against sins committed in secret.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r4.anchor: أي ما يختلج في سره وقلبه وضميره، وفي هذا زجر عن المعاصي التي يستخفى بها

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r5.claim: Waswasa is inner self-talk, like quiet speech; al-Aʿshā’s line uses waswās for the faint sound of jewelry.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r5.anchor: والوسوسة حديث النفس بمنزلة الكلام الخفي. قال الأعشى: تسمع للحلي وسواسا إذا انصرفت

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r6.claim: The jugular is the neck vein extending from the throat toward the shoulder, with one on each side; this is standard Arabic usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r6.anchor: هو حبل العاتق وهو ممتد من ناحية حلقه إلى عاتقه، وهما وريدان عن يمين وشمال. روى معناه عن ابن عباس وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r7.claim: The expression joins two words for the same thing: the cord is the vein, with the wording varied.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r7.anchor: والحبل هو الوريد فأضيف إلى نفسه لاختلاف اللفظين

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the warīd as the watīn, a vein attached to the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: الوريد الوتين وهو عرق معلق بالقلب

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r9.claim: The comparison depicts nearness figuratively, not nearness in physical distance.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r9.anchor: وهذا تمثيل للقرب أي نحن أقرب إليه من حبل وريده الذي هو منه، وليس على وجه قرب المسافة

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r10.claim: Another interpretation is that God has more control over a person than his own jugular vein, despite the person’s control of it.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r10.anchor: وقيل أي ونحن أملك به من حبل وريده مع استيلائه عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r11.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r11.claim: A further reading makes the nearness one of knowledge and power: God knows a person’s whispers more intimately than the heart does, and nothing hides His knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:50:16-17/r11.anchor: روي معناه عن مقاتل قال: الوريد عرق يخالط القلب، وهذا القرب قرب العلم والقدرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p445/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p445/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p445/r4.claim: The next passage moves from the recording of deeds and words to Judgment and the criminals, their casting into Hell and mutual cursing, then to the blessings prepared for the righteous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p445/r4.anchor: In the succeeding verses, first the elaborate arrangement made by the Almighty in recording the deeds and words of a person is mentioned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r1.claim: Doubts about reviving the dead and recording every hidden and open deed are two sides of one objection; verse 4 briefly answers both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r1.anchor: Both these doubts are two sides of the same coin. For this reason, in verse 4 earlier both are briefly answered.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r2.claim: Because God created man, He knows even the thoughts in his heart, let alone his words and deeds; this answers doubt about how every act could be recorded for judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p446/r2.anchor: The verse says that it is God Who has created man and even what comes in his heart is also known to God, let alone his words and deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r1.claim: A creator must know every detail of his creatures; otherwise, Islahi argues, how could God arrange for their protection and sustenance? The cited Qur’anic question is at 67:14.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r1.anchor: If a Creator is not aware of all the minute details of His creatures, how can He make arrangements for their protection and sustenance?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r2.claim: Warīd means the life vein and is a common Arabic idiom for extreme nearness; God’s knowledge and power encompass each person, seen and unseen.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p447/r2.anchor: This is a very common Arabic idiom which is used to express extreme nearness.
